hero.subtitle: From the Primordial Waters of Creation
hero.title: The Infinite Cycle
hero.lore: Before time, before earth, before the sky was woven — there was only the endless dark water. From its depths rose Ak Ana, the White Mother, carrying the breath of creation — Kut. She whispered, and the cosmos stirred into being.
hero.youAreHere: You stand at the heart of this story: the Middle World — the steppe, the hearth, mortal life. Above lies the sky and mercy; below, trial and the underworld; Bayterek is the axis that binds them all.

migration.heading: The Path of
migration.desc: Follow the Celestial Grey Wolf across the iron mountains and endless steppes — from imprisonment to liberation, from winter's grip to spring's rebirth.

ergenekon.title: Ergenekon
ergenekon.subtitle: The Iron Mountain Prison
ergenekon.text: After a devastating defeat, the surviving Turkic tribes retreated into a hidden valley enclosed by impassable iron mountains. For generations they forged their identity in the fires of patience.

goc.title: The Great Migration
goc.subtitle: Birth of Empires
goc.text: When a blacksmith melted the iron mountain with a great forge, the Turkic people poured forth like a river of steel, reborn and unstoppable. Guided by Gökbörü, the Celestial Wolf.

steppes.title: The Endless Steppes
steppes.subtitle: Home of the Free
steppes.text: Across the vast grasslands of Central Asia they spread — horse-riders, sky-worshippers, keepers of the wolf banner. Each tribe carrying the sacred fire of Tengri.

worldTree.heading: Bayterek
worldTree.p1: At the center of all existence stands Bayterek — the sacred World Tree whose roots descend into the Abyss of Tamag, whose trunk sustains the mortal realm of the Steppes, and whose branches reach into the celestial palace of Tengri.
worldTree.p2: The World Tree is the axis of all cosmology — a bridge between gods and mortals, between life and death. Every soul, every spirit, every saga flows through its veins.
worldTree.axisNote: The trunk stands in the middle world; branches reach the sky, roots sink into Tamag.
worldTree.visitorBlurb: As you scroll, you move from sky to steppe to depth — yet you always begin from the human world; the mythology turns around that vantage point.
worldTree.upperDesc: Ülgen and the sky layers. Kut and mercy flow from this realm toward earth.
worldTree.middleDesc: The steppe, creatures, and mortal life — the breath at the center of the cosmos.
worldTree.lowerDesc: Erlik Khan's realm — where trial, death, and the paths of return meet.

ritual.heading: The Ritual
ritual.desc: The shamanic drum is the bridge between worlds. Each symbol opens a portal to the spirits that guard nature, water, and the forgotten realms.
ritual.drumDesc: Click the symbols to reveal the hidden guardians

sun.name: Kün — The Sun
sun.lore: The eye of Tengri, the Eternal Blue Sky. The sun watches over the Upper World and bestows Kut — divine life force — upon the worthy. Shamans journey toward the sun during their celestial ascent.

moon.name: Ay — The Moon
moon.lore: Guardian of the night and keeper of dreams. The moon governs the tides of the spirit world. Under its light, the veil between worlds grows thin and shamans can commune with the dead.

tree.name: Bayterek — World Tree
tree.lore: The axis of all cosmology. Through the drum, shamans climb the World Tree — ascending its seventeen branches to reach the realm of Ülgen, or descending its roots to negotiate with Erlik Han.

wolf.name: Börü — The Wolf
wolf.lore: Sacred guide and ancestor spirit. The wolf on the drum represents Asena, the divine she-wolf who birthed the Turkic people. Shamans call upon her spirit for protection and guidance.

eagle.name: Kartal — The Eagle
eagle.lore: Messenger between worlds. The eagle carries prayers from the Middle World to Tengri's throne. The first shaman was said to have been raised by an eagle in the crown of Bayterek.

water.name: Su — The Water
water.lore: The primordial element from which all creation emerged. Su İyesi, the Water Spirit, dwells in every river, lake, and spring. Offerings of milk and bread ensure her blessing.

suIyesi.name: Su İyesi — Water Guardian
suIyesi.desc: She dwells in every river, lake, and spring. Beautiful and terrifying, she can grant fertile harvests or drag the unworthy into the depths. Fishermen whisper prayers before casting their nets.
suIyesi.offering: Offerings: Milk, bread, and silver coins at the water's edge

ormanIyesi.name: Orman İyesi — Forest Guardian
ormanIyesi.desc: Master of every tree, root, and creature of the wild. He appears as a towering figure of bark and moss, or a whispering wind through the canopy. Those who respect the forest receive his protection.
ormanIyesi.warning: Warning: Never cut a tree without asking the Forest Spirit's permission

sun.title: Gün Ana — Sun Mother
sun.desc: The life-giving solar deity, revered as the source of warmth and light. She dwells in the highest celestial layer.

moon.title: Ay Ata — Moon Father
moon.desc: The ancestral guardian of the night, guiding nomadic paths across the endless steppes and ruling the tides.
moon.offering: Warning: Never point at the full moon.

eagle.title: Karakuş — Divine Eagle
eagle.desc: The messenger of the heavens. It carries prayers to Kayra Han and watches over the sacred mountains.

tree.title: Bayterek — World Tree
tree.desc: The cosmic axis connecting the underworld, earth, and heavens. It channels energy across dimensions.

wolf.title: Kökbörü — Sky Wolf
wolf.desc: The divine guide of the Turkic peoples, leading them out of Ergenekon. A symbol of resilience and freedom.
wolf.offering: The eternal spirit of the pack.

water.title: Su İyesi — Water Guardian
water.desc: She dwells in every river, lake, and spring. Beautiful and terrifying, she can grant fertile harvests or drag the unworthy into the depths.
water.offering: Offerings: Silver coins at the waters edge.

forest.title: Orman İyesi — Forest Guardian
forest.desc: Master of every tree, root, and creature of the wild. He appears as a whispering wind through the canopy.
forest.offering: Warning: Never cut a tree without asking permission.

ritual.iyelerDesc: The invisible but ever-present masters of mountains, rivers, and forests. Show them respect, and they will protect you.

kayberen.name: The Lost Saints
kayberen.desc: Sacred, invisible spirits dwelling on the highest mountain peaks. They protect wildlife and the innocent. Those who disrespect their mountains will lose their way.
kayberen.lore1: The Kayberens (the "Lost Saints") are holy, radiant beings invisible to human eyes. In Kyrgyz and Kazakh legend they dwell on the highest mountain peaks, protect herds of wild animals and bring abundance. In winter they show the way through the mountains to nomads whose hearts are pure.
kayberen.lore2: They lend a helping hand to innocent people in trouble. Those who disrespect the mountains they guard, kill a young animal for sport or defile the forest are swallowed by a sudden enchanted mist and lose their way, and their minds, forever.

suyla.name: Suyla
suyla.desc: A mythical spirit born from fragments of the Sun and Moon. With horse-like eyes, an eagle's beak, and serpentine hair, it carries humanity's prayers to the divine.
suyla.lore1: Suyla is one of the most important binding figures of shamanic ritual. Tengri created it from the first crumbs of light of the Sun and the Moon. It has the smooth eyes of a horse, the sharp beak of an eagle and wavy golden hair like serpents.
suyla.lore2: When people hold great sacrificial rites or shamans fall into trance, it is the winged Suyla that carries the blood, the prayer and the offering to the highest reaches of the sky. Without Suyla, no wish can reach Ülgen.
suyla.connection: Envoy of the Shamans · Voice of the Sky

suIyesi.name: Water Spirit
suIyesi.desc: She dwells in every river, lake, and spring. Beautiful and terrifying; she can grant fertile harvests or drag the unworthy into the depths.
suIyesi.lore1: In Turkic culture water is not merely an element but a sacred being that lives, breathes and remembers. The Water Spirit is the embodiment of this spring of life. It usually appears as an enchanting, luminous long-haired figure bathing on the surface of the water.
suIyesi.lore2: Those who throw stones into rivers, pollute the waters or gaze disrespectfully at their reflection at night suffer the Water Spirit's wrath and are dragged into bottomless whirlpools. Travellers who wish to please it leave silver coins or red ribbons in the water.
suIyesi.connection: Blood of the Steppe · Ruler of the Depths

ormanIyesi.name: Forest Spirit
ormanIyesi.desc: Master of every tree, root, and wild creature. He appears as a towering figure covered in bark and moss, or as a whisper through the canopy.
ormanIyesi.lore1: The Forest Spirit is the living soul of every leaf, every great beech and every fallen log on the forest floor. For the steppe peoples the forest is dark and dangerous, yet a single tree felled with the Forest Spirit's permission brings kut and warmth to the home.
ormanIyesi.lore2: It confuses hunters who harm animals needlessly and lures them into the deepest darkness of the woods. Some legends describe it as a shape-shifting stag or a giant shaggy bear. It also guards the earthly trunk of Bayterek, the heart of the forest.
ormanIyesi.connection: Key of Nature · Warden of Bayterek

pantheon.heading: The Divine
pantheon.desc: The gods who shaped the cosmos and govern the fate of every soul beneath the Eternal Blue Sky.

mergen.name: Mergen
mergen.desc: Dwelling in the 7th layer of heaven, he is the all-knowing deity whose sacred arrow never misses its mark. He grants wisdom and intellect to humanity.
mergen.lore1: In Turkic mythology Mergen Khan is the symbol of reason, awareness and sound judgement. He dwells on the seventh layer of the sky and is held to be one of the greatest sages guiding human fate. His sacred bow and arrow stand not only for hitting the mark but for truth and justice.
mergen.lore2: He is one of Kayra Khan's sons. Rather than the battlefield, he is believed to have taught people to think, to overcome hardship with wit and to build civilisation. Before making a difficult decision, shamans ask Mergen Khan for guidance on their spirit journeys.
mergen.connection: Son of Kayra Khan · Light of Intellect

kayra.name: Kayra Han
kayra.desc: The supreme creator who existed before all. Father of Ülgen and Erlik, he shaped the two brothers and set them upon their eternal paths — one to light, one to darkness.
kayra.lore1: In the Altai creation epics, when there was not yet a universe, an earth or a sky, Kayra Khan was the only power, flying over the 'Endless Water'. He is said to have shaped the universe with his first thought and the souls with his breath.
kayra.lore2: Above the whole pantheon, on the seventeenth layer of the sky, he dwells in unreachable splendour. He does not keep the balance of the universe himself; instead, by setting his sons Ülgen on the path of good and Erlik on the path of evil and trial, he began the eternal dance of darkness and light.
kayra.connection: Summit of the Pantheon · Source of Creation

ulgen.name: Ülgen
ulgen.desc: Ruler of the Upper World with seven sons who embody the elements of nature. Ülgen guides shamans through the sky's seventeen layers and bestows the sacred Kut upon the worthy.
ulgen.lore1: In Tengrism, Ülgen is the main source of goodness, mercy and abundance. He sits on a golden throne atop the Golden Mountain on the sixteenth layer of the sky. He is known as the god who taught people fire, reason, farming and the arts.
ulgen.lore2: He is locked in an endless cosmic struggle for balance with Erlik Khan, lord of evil. Ülgen does not act alone: together with his seven sons, who rule the heavenly bodies and the weather, and his nine daughters (the White Maidens) who protect people, he spreads mercy over the earth.
ulgen.connection: Erlik's Eternal Rival · Giver of Fire

kyzagan.name: Kyzagan
kyzagan.desc: Son of Ülgen and guardian of warriors. Kyzagan rides the crimson storm, his blazing sword cleaving the sky. He blesses armies with courage and judges the valor of fallen heroes.
kyzagan.lore1: As his name suggests, Kızagan is the divine embodiment of anger, fury and relentless war. He descends upon battlefields above red clouds, riding a giant crimson camel. He is said to appear as a blazing aura at the very front of armies.
kyzagan.lore2: Before setting out on campaign, old Turkic warriors turned to him, and through him to Tengri, for strength and courage. Kızagan knows no mercy and respects only strength and honour. Ruthless towards the enemy, he honours the souls of heroes who died for their homeland in the realm of warriors.
kyzagan.connection: Son of Ülgen · Kut of War

umay.name: Umay Ana
umay.desc: Divine mother of birth, fertility, protection, and life. The celestial goddess who holds the thread of Tengri and safeguards every newborn soul into the world.
umay.loreTitle: Spirit of the Tree of Life
umay.lore1: In Turkic and Altai mythology Umay Ana is the most important and most loving sacred force that keeps life going. She is often depicted as a graceful woman in a pure white dress, with silver hair and a horned headdress. Through her heavenly blessing the earth breathes and flourishes.
umay.lore2: She protects children, mothers and young animals in particular from evil spirits and the dark influence of the underworld. Since the time of the Huns, Göktürks and Uyghurs she has been the most revered being, named right after Gök Tengri. When a baby smiles in its sleep, it is said that Umay Ana is speaking to it.
umay.connection: Enemy of Darkness · Protector of Life

pantheon.nexusDesc: Hover over a deity to reveal their connections and influence over the realms

akAna.name: Ak Ana
akAna.desc: The radiant White Mother who rises from the endless waters before time. She calls out “Create!” to Kayra Khan and so begins the creation of the universe.

erlik.name: Erlik Khan
erlik.desc: The first being exiled from the sky, master of death and of Tamag. Beneath the nine-branched black pine he judges the souls of the dead.
erlik.lore1: At the dawn of creation Erlik stood beside Kayra Khan, but for his pride and his desire to create worlds of his own he was punished and exiled to the underworld (Tamag). In this lightless realm he sits on a silver throne beneath a rootless, nine-branched black pine, ruling shadows and sickness.
erlik.lore2: While Ülgen taught people fire and goodness, Erlik Khan taught them death, sin and craftsmanship. With his dark-mounted messengers, demonic shamans and the vast spirit army known as the Abasi, he keeps the earth under constant trial. His power is an undeniable cosmic necessity.
erlik.connection: Kayra Khan's Rebel · Shadow of Absolute Justice

bestiary.heading: Bestiary of the
bestiary.desc: Creatures and spirits that roam between the realms — companions of heroes, products of curses, and guardians of nature.

itbarak.name: Itbarak
itbarak.desc: A legendary race of fierce warriors with human bodies and dog heads, mentioned in the Epic of Oghuz Khagan.
itbarak.lore1: They were so savage and powerful that they defeated the great Oghuz Khagan's army in their first encounter.
itbarak.lore2: Later, Oghuz Khagan gathered his strength, returned, and vanquished this dark tribe, making them a terrifying steppe legend.

bukre.name: Bukre
bukre.desc: Divine steed of legendary heroes, Bukre soars between the clouds on feathered wings of pure light.
bukre.lore1: Bukre is a dragon-like creature in Turkic mythology, often depicted as a winged horse or a powerful steed with magical abilities. It is said to be the companion of heroes and a symbol of strength and courage.
bukre.lore2: In the sagas of Manas and Oghuz, the Bukre carries its rider through impossible battles and across the boundaries between the living and the dead.
bukre.connection: Companion of Heroes · Cursed by Erlik Khan

tulpar.name: Tulpar
tulpar.desc: Divine steed of legendary heroes, Tulpar soars between the clouds on feathered wings of pure light.
tulpar.lore1: Born from the tears of Ülgen when he wept for banished heroes, the Tulpar is the most sacred companion a warrior can earn. Only those deemed worthy by the Sky God may ride upon its back through the seventeen layers of heaven.
tulpar.lore2: In the sagas of Manas and Oghuz, the Tulpar carries its rider through impossible battles and across the boundaries between the living and the dead.
tulpar.connection: Companion of Heroes · Blessed by Ülgen

tepegoz.name: Tepegöz
tepegoz.desc: A terrifying cyclops born of a curse, terrorizing the Oghuz tribes until Basat the hero defeats it.
tepegoz.lore1: Tepegöz was born from an unnatural union between a shepherd and a Peri (fairy). The creature grew into an unstoppable giant with a single eye, devouring sixty men per day.
tepegoz.lore2: Only the hero Basat — raised by a lion and blessed with divine courage — could face the beast and pierce its single eye with a red-hot iron stake.
tepegoz.connection: Product of a Curse · Slain by Basat

arcura.name: Arçura
arcura.desc: Guardian of the wild, Arçura lures wanderers into the deep forest and can grant wisdom — or madness.
arcura.lore1: Arçura dwells in the deepest, most ancient forests of the Turkic lands. She appears in many forms — sometimes as a beautiful maiden, sometimes as a towering figure covered in bark and moss.
arcura.lore2: Shamans would commune with Arçura to gain knowledge of medicinal herbs and the spirits of nature.

asena.name: Asena
asena.desc: Sacred mother wolf of the Turkic peoples, she nursed the last surviving boy and gave birth to ten tribes.
asena.lore1: When enemies slaughtered the entire Turkic tribe, a single wounded boy was left for dead. A celestial she-wolf, Asena, found the child and nursed him back to health in a hidden valley surrounded by mountains.
asena.lore2: Asena is the most sacred symbol of Turkic identity — the divine wolf who ensured the survival and rebirth of an entire civilization. The wolf banner flies at the front of every great army.
asena.connection: Mother of Tribes · Blessed by Tengri

alkarisi.name: Alkarisi
alkarisi.desc: One of Erlik Khan's oldest shadows on earth. Often depicted in red garments, targeting fresh life energy and carrying souls to the lord of the underworld.
alkarisi.lore1: Alkarisi is a malicious spirit sent to earth by Erlik Khan. She primarily haunts women in childbirth and newborns. She is known for her red garments and long hair, though her face is often terrifying.
alkarisi.lore2: She works to harvest human life energy. She drags her victims to underground dungeons to strengthen Erlik Khan's army. Shamans keep her away using iron, Syrian rue, and the color red.

abasi.name: Abasi
abasi.desc: They form Erlik Khan’s vast host of evil spirits — one-eyed, one-legged, or toothless. They spread illness and drag souls toward Tamag’s dungeons.
abasi.lore1: The Abasi are among Erlik Khan’s most faithful servants in the underworld. Each embodies a different kind of harm or sickness. Some have a single eye, some a single leg, some terrible teeth.
abasi.lore2: They steal life energy and trap souls in underworld prisons. Shamans use iron objects and powerful prayers to drive them back.

kamos.name: Kamos
kamos.desc: A dark force that presses upon sleepers at night. Erlik Khan uses it to seize people in their most vulnerable hour.
kamos.lore1: Kamos is a dark being sent to earth by Erlik Khan. At night it settles on sleepers, paralyzes them, steals their breath, and fills their minds with nightmares.
kamos.lore2: Shamans use metal objects and strong prayers to keep Kamos away, and try to keep victims awake until the danger passes.

kayberen.name: Kayberenler
kayberen.desc: Invisible guardian spirits of the mountains and forests. They protect nature, wildlife, and the innocent.
kayberen.lore1: Kayberenler (Missing Saints) are invisible, sacred, and radiant beings. According to Kyrgyz and Kazakh legends, they live on the highest peaks of mountains, protect wild animal herds, and bring abundance.
kayberen.lore2: They extent a helping hand to the innocent in distress. Those who disrespect the mountains where they reside will lose their way. In Anatolian beliefs, they are equated with saints in human form.

azmic.name: Azmıç
azmic.desc: In Turkic and Balkar tradition, an evil spirit that preys on lone travelers. It has no fixed form; it calls in a familiar voice. Turning back to answer leads the victim astray.
azmic.lore1: Azmıç (also named Aznıç, Azıtkı) is known as a road spirit or lost soul. It shifts shape and may appear as someone the victim loves. It chooses those who walk alone.
azmic.lore2: Whoever turns to answer the call falls under its power; it leads them over cliffs, into ravines, or rivers. The name echoes the root 'az-' — to lead astray. In speech it is sometimes confused with similar-sounding words.
azmic.connection: Peril of the Lonely Road · Shape-Shifting Spirit

jeztirnak.name: Jeztırnak
jeztirnak.desc: In Turkic and Caucasus oral tradition, an evil spirit known for long, iron-like nails. It scratches at doors in the dead of night, preying on lone households and travelers; those who heed its sounds are filled with dread.
jeztirnak.lore1: Jeztırnak is tied to claw and nail imagery. Tales place it on a roof or beside a lonely road; victims hear a metallic tapping or scraping as it draws near.
jeztirnak.lore2: Iron, salt, prayers, and shamanic practice are said to keep it at bay. Some stories link it to Erlik Khan’s shadows; its true leverage is fear and solitude.
jeztirnak.connection: Night Visitor · Legend of the Iron Claw

yegi.name: Yegi
yegi.desc: A dark being associated with the underworld. It is felt at the edge of sleep or in moments of sharp fear — tightening the breath and clouding the mind.
yegi.lore1: Narratives describe Yegi as a spirit from Tamag’s gloom or among Erlik Khan’s host. It may have no fixed form: sometimes mist, sometimes a shadow in the corner of a ceiling.
yegi.lore2: Traditional protection — iron, cleansing prayers, sleeping among others — is said to blunt its reach. It is thought to choose those who are alone or weakened.
yegi.connection: Shadow of Tamag · Foe of Rest

bestiary.noResultsDesc: No such spirit is known in the depths of the ancient forests and realms.

shadow.heading: SHADOW
shadow.desc: Ancient depths where the first seeds of darkness were sown, ruled by silence and judgment.
shadow.erlikP1: Absolute ruler of the underworld in Turkic mythology. The first being exiled from the heavens and the lord of death.
shadow.erlikP2: Guardian of darkness and balance, sitting beneath the nine-branched black pine with his silver staff.
shadow.exploreIntro: Erlik Khan’s most often told emissaries of Tamag — jump straight to their entry.
shadow.alkarisiDesc: A malevolent spirit that haunts postpartum women, stealing their life energy (Kut).
shadow.alkarisiLore2: Drawn to the vulnerable, particularly during childbirth.

bukre.name: Bukre
bukre.desc: A wise, wingless dragon representing goodness and balance, known for battling the evil dragon Sangal.
bukre.title: Legend of Bukre
bukre.lore2: A guardian of the underworld's deepest secrets, snaking through Tamag.

shadow.karaburaDesc: The being that guards Erlik Han’s iron forges in the underworld and carries the dark energy.
shadow.judgmentDesc: The underworld justice that decides the eternal journey of souls within Tamag.

kulliyat.title: DARK
kulliyat.subtitle: The secret history of malevolent spirits and ancient creatures shaped by the will of Erlik Khan.
kulliyat.footer: This information is compiled from ancient Turkic mythological sources.

alkarisi.title: Alkarisi
alkarisi.desc: One of Erlik Khan's oldest shadows on earth. Often depicted in red garments, targeting fresh life energy and carrying souls to the lord of the underworld.
alkarisi.weak: Iron, the color red, and Syrian rue.

abasi.title: Abasi
abasi.desc: They form Erlik Khan’s vast host of evil spirits — one-eyed, one-legged, or toothless. They spread illness and drag souls toward Tamag’s dungeons.

kamos.title: Kamos
kamos.desc: A dark force that presses upon sleepers at night. Erlik Khan uses it to seize people in their most vulnerable hour.

bukre.title: BÜKRE
bukre.desc: One of the mightiest and wisest dragon figures in Turkic mythology, known for its legendary battles with Sangal, the evil dragon. It is depicted as a giant, legless serpent. Bükre stands for goodness and strength, descending to the earth every nine years to restore order and balance.
bukre.weak: The absolute dominion of evil and Sangal's dark magic.

sagas.heading: The Epic
sagas.desc: Tales woven into the very fabric of the steppes — of iron mountains, divine wolves, and the unbreakable spirit of a people.

ergenekon.title: The Saga of Ergenekon
ergenekon.p1: After a devastating defeat, the surviving Turkic tribes retreated into Ergenekon — a hidden valley enclosed by impassable iron mountains. For generations they lived in isolation, growing strong and numerous, forging their identity in the fires of patience.
ergenekon.p2: When the valley could no longer hold them, a blacksmith melted the iron mountain itself with a great forge. The Turkic people poured forth like a river of steel, reborn and unstoppable. The day of their emergence is celebrated as Nevruz — the New Day.
ergenekon.p3: This new generation that came down from the mountains into the valleys was armed with the wisdom of the past and the sharpness of the sword. The exodus from Ergenekon was not just a physical escape; it is the epic of a civilisation reborn from its ashes and returning in glory to the world. This awakening, which struck fear into enemies and hope into friends, became a lasting symbol of freedom.

oghuz.title: The Epic of Oghuz Khagan
oghuz.p1: Oghuz Khagan was born with the face of the sky, the strength of the mountain, and the heart of the wolf. From infancy, he spoke to eagles and commanded rivers. He conquered the four corners of the world, guided by a divine grey wolf.
oghuz.p2: He divided his empire among his six sons — three of the Sun (Bozok) and three of the Moon (Üçok) — creating the foundation of all great Turkic dynasties that would shape the world for millennia.
oghuz.p3: With his divine first wife, who appeared within a great light descending from the sky, and his second wife, born of a great tree on the earth, Oghuz united earth and sky. The line that spread from his son Gün Khan carried the most merciful yet most unbending blood of the steppe. With the command "Let the sky be our tent and the sun our banner", Oghuz began the ideal of world dominion.

asena.title: The Legend of Asena & The Great Migration
asena.p1: When enemies destroyed the Turkic people, only a single boy survived, grievously wounded. A celestial she-wolf, Asena, found the dying child and nursed him in a secret cave among the Altai Mountains.
asena.p2: From their divine bond came ten sons — each the father of a great Turkic tribe. When the population outgrew the sacred valley, they migrated across the vast steppes of Central Asia, carrying the wolf banner as their eternal symbol.
asena.p3: This migration was no ordinary march; it was a people's effort to reunite with its roots. Asena's sacred milk instilled in Turkic blood not only salvation but also the free spirit of the wolves. From that day on, whenever the first moonlight on the horizon turned blood-red, the great howl of the grey wolf echoed like an anthem from the mountain peaks to the plains.

manas.title: The Epic of Manas
manas.p1: The greatest oral epic in history, sung across the Kyrgyz steppes for over a thousand years. Manas was chosen by Tengri himself — a warrior-hero of divine fury, destined to unite the forty scattered Kyrgyz tribes against the armies that sought to erase them from the earth.
manas.p2: Spanning three generations — Manas, his son Semetey, and grandson Seytek — this monumental cycle is twenty times longer than Homer's Iliad. It is not merely a story; it is the living soul of a people, chanted by sacred bards called Manaschi who enter a trance state to summon the hero's spirit.
manas.p3: Manas's birth caused a red glow in the sky and great storms on the earth. His gallop against the wind on his faithful horse Akkula heralded that he would become the protector of the oppressed. Growing into a giant on the battlefield with his forty warriors, Manas upheld justice with his sword and exalted custom with his fairness.

umaySection.heading: Umay
umaySection.desc: Divine mother of birth, fertility, and protection. The invisible celestial shield that Tengri bestows upon every living soul.
umaySection.lore1: Umay Ana dwells in the brightest layer of the sky and weaves an invisible shield of protection around every newborn soul at the moment of birth. This celestial young goddess, dressed in white with a silver-handled staff and a golden crown, is the companion of Kayra Han and the eternal source of abundance.
umaySection.lore2: Shamans call upon her during child illnesses, births, and any ritual requiring protection. Her offerings include golden silk, milk, and white fur. The soul under her protection carries a celestial armor unreachable by any underworld entity.
umaySection.connection1Desc: She lives under Tengri's blessing. During births and the growth of abundance she embodies Tengri's will on earth.
umaySection.connection2Desc: She is the most powerful celestial shield that prevents Alkarisi and Abasailers from haunting the newborn.
umaySection.offering: Offerings: White silk, milk, and golden embroidery.

ergenekon.p1: After a devastating defeat, only two persons from the Turkic tribes, Kiyan and Nukuz, and their wives remained. While fleeing from the enemies, they found a passage between steep mountains so narrow that only a deer could pass.
ergenekon.p2: When they passed through this passage, they found a secret and paradise-like valley surrounded by impassable high mountains, where rivers, fruit trees, and game animals were abundant. They named this place Ergenekon, meaning 'mine place'.
ergenekon.p3: They lived in Ergenekon for four hundred years and multiplied so much that they could no longer fit in this valley. They could not find the narrow passage their ancestors used to come here. While exploring the surroundings of the mountains, they noticed that there was iron ore in only one place.
ergenekon.p4: A blacksmith said that this mountain could be melted. They lined up a row of wood and a row of coal around the mountain. They made huge bellows from seventy hides. When they pulled the bellows together, the fire became so fierce that the iron mountain melted and a road large enough for a loaded camel to pass was opened.
ergenekon.p5: That day became the day of rebirth for the Turks. They emerged from Ergenekon under the guidance of a celestial Grey Wolf (Gökböri) and dominated all the steppes again by taking revenge on their ancestors.
ergenekon.title: THE EPIC OF ERGENEKON
ergenekon.subtitle: Prison of the Iron Mountain

oghuz.title: THE EPIC OF OGHUZ KHAGAN
oghuz.subtitle: The Sky-Faced Khagan
oghuz.p1: Oghuz Khagan was born as a child with a face blue like the sky, a mouth red like fire, and eyes bright like diamonds. He started to speak, walk, and eat raw meat when he was only forty days old. As the shadow of Tengri on earth, he was a master of using all kinds of weapons.
oghuz.p2: One day, he killed a huge monster (Kiyant) that threatened his people by himself. After this victory, he married a divine woman who appeared in a beam of light. He had three sons from her named Sun, Moon, and Star. Later, he married another woman he found in a tree hollow and had three sons from her named Sky, Mountain, and Sea.
oghuz.p3: One day, while Oghuz Khagan was on a campaign with his army, a large male wolf with a celestial mane appeared before him. The wolf said, 'O Oghuz, wherever you go, I will walk before you.' The Turkic army followed this divine guide and conquered the four corners of the world.
oghuz.p4: When Oghuz Khagan grew old, he distributed his golden bow and three silver arrows among his sons. He divided his country into Bozoks and Uchoks. He advised his children to stay in unity and solidarity. His legacy became the foundation of the great Turkic dynasties that would rule for millennia.

asena.title: THE LEGEND OF ASENA & THE GREAT MIGRATION
asena.subtitle: The Sacred Wolf of Rebirth
asena.p1: In ancient times, the Turkic tribes were subjected to a large enemy attack. All the people were slaughtered, only a small child with his arms and legs cut off was left behind. The enemies left him in a swamp, thinking he would die.
asena.p2: Asena, a she-wolf descended from the sky, found the child and healed his wounds by licking them. She ensured his growth by feeding him with meat every day. When the child grew up, he became the mate of the wolf. When the enemies found out that the child was alive and came to kill him, Asena flew and took refuge in a hidden cave among the Altai Mountains.
asena.p3: Behind the cave was a paradise-like valley. Asena gave birth to ten boys there. These boys grew up and married girls from outside, forming the ten great Turkic tribes. Their lineage multiplied so much that they could no longer fit in the valley.
asena.p4: Under the guidance of the Divine Wolf, they decided to leave the valley and migrate to the open steppes. Carrying the wolf banner at the front, they returned to the lands of their ancestors. This great migration was the beginning of the eternal dominance of the Turks in the steppes.

manas.title: THE EPIC OF MANAS
manas.subtitle: The Eternal Champion of the Steppes
manas.p1: Manas was not merely born — he was forged. Before his birth, his father Jakıp dreamed of a great eagle descending from the sky, dropping a sword of crimson fire into his hands. The shamans declared: a champion would come who would unite all scattered Kyrgyz tribes and shake the very foundations of the earth.
manas.p2: As a child Manas could not be contained. He defeated grown men in combat, tamed wild horses with a single roar, and spoke to Tengri directly in his dreams. He was given the sacred armor — the great coat of forty skins — and the legendary warhorses Ak Kula and Gülayım, companions gifted by the spirit world.
manas.p3: Manas did not rise alone. Around him gathered the Kyrk Choro — the Forty Heroes — warriors of mythic power, each carrying a divine gift. Almambet, born under a star that no astrologer could name, mastered the weather and rode storms like cavalry. Chubak's war cry could scatter armies before a single sword was drawn.
manas.p4: Together they fought the Kalmyks, the Khitans, and every force that sought to erase the Kyrgyz people. Manas stormed the great fortified city of Bejin, broke its iron gates with his bare hands, and returned with the treasures of forty kingdoms. But greatness draws envy — even from within.
manas.p5: Manas died not on the battlefield but from poisoned wounds dealt by betrayal. Yet even in death he did not end. His wife Kanıkey hid his true tomb, and his legend became the epic's lifeblood — sung by Manaschi bards in a sacred trance for over a thousand years, ensuring the hero lives forever in the voice of his people.

terms.def: The divine life force, abundance, and blessing bestowed by Tengri.
The Underworld. The dark realm of torment ruled by Erlik Khan.
The divine region in the highest heavenly layer where Tengri resides.
The legendary World Tree connecting the underworld, earth, and sky.
The realm of mortals — steppe, camp, and hearth. It rests at Bayterek's trunk between the upper and lower worlds.
Human beings seeking Kut — living between grace from above and trial from below.
A malevolent road spirit in Turkic and Balkar lore. It calls to lone travelers in a familiar voice; turning back to answer means being led astray. Also known as Aznıç or Azıtkı.
The eternal blue sky, creator of the universe and the supreme power.
Spiritual leader who communicates with the spirit world, heals, and leads rituals.
Guardian spirits of entities in nature (water, mountain, forest, etc.). The Master/Owner.

akAna.name: Ak Ana
akAna.desc: In the Altai creation story, the radiant White Mother who rises from the endless waters that covered everything before time. She calls out "Create!" to Kayra Khan, who was alone and uncertain, and so begins the creation of the universe before sinking back into the depths.

cosmos.title: Cosmology
cosmos.desc: In old Turkic belief the universe is made of three layers bound together by Bayterek. Tap a layer to discover the beings who dwell there.

sky.title: Sky
sky.desc: The realm of light and goodness. In Altai tradition the heavens rise layer upon layer; Ülgen sits in his golden palace on the sixteenth layer and Kayra Khan dwells at the very top. At the centre of the sky stands the Iron Stake (the Pole Star), around which the heavens turn.
facts: The Iron Stake: nail of the sky
The shaman's ascent to the heavens

middle.title: Earth
middle.desc: Home of humans, animals and guardian spirits. The sacred Yer-Sub (land and water) honoured in the Orkhon Inscriptions is filled with the spirits of mountains, rivers and forests. Humankind is charged with keeping the balance between sky and underworld.
facts: Spirits of mountain, water and forest
Wolf, horse and eagle: blessed animals
Bayterek's trunk rises from this world

under.title: Underworld
under.desc: The dark land of Erlik Khan. In the underworld, which descends layer by layer, the souls of the dead are judged; Erlik's servants and dark spirits carry sickness and nightmares to the surface. Shamans descend here only at great peril.
